c.tagline: Fiji's tourism gateway, where beach resorts meet a bustling market town.

taxi.color: varies (often white or silver, with rooftop taxi sign)
taxi.fareNote: Meters exist but many drivers negotiate a flat fare, especially airport-to-resort trips; confirm price before departing.

emergency.note: 917 covers police and ambulance dispatch nationwide; some hotels also keep direct lines to Nadi's Lautoka Hospital or private clinics.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Denarau Island: Port Denarau Marina, Denarau Island, Fiji

avoid.reason: Opportunistic theft around the town and beaches; caution at night

hood_desc: A manicured resort peninsula packed with international beach resorts, a marina, and a golf course; best for honeymooners and families wanting an all-inclusive, self-contained beach holiday.
A laid-back local beach strip with grey-gold sand, budget guesthouses and backpacker hostels; suits travelers wanting a cheap, social, walk-to-the-beach base with sunset views.

Nadi's main tourist strip along Queens Road with the highest density of restaurants, bars, curry houses and mid-range hotels; convenient for travelers without a car who want nightlife and easy transport links.
The compact downtown core with the produce market, handicraft shops, temples and mosques; good for budget travelers wanting an authentic local-city feel and easy bus/onward-travel connections.
A cluster of business-class hotels and a golf course a few minutes from the terminal; ideal for late arrivals/early departures or stopovers who prioritize airport proximity over beach access.
lodging: Radisson Blu Resort Fiji Denarau Island

water.note: Treated municipal water can still carry bacterial contamination; resorts recommend bottled water for visitors.

transit.pay: Local buses are paid in cash to the driver or conductor on boarding (small FJD coins for short hops); there is no citywide tap card. Resort/Denarau shuttle buses and island ferries are usually booked and paid for in advance online or through hotel tour desks.
transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 6am-9pm with reduced evening frequency; no true late-night service, so taxis are the main option after dark.
transit.note: Buses are cheap and frequent along the Queens Road corridor (Airport-Martintar-Nadi Town-Lautoka) but have no fixed published route map; ferries to the Mamanuca/Yasawa islands depart from Port Denarau Marina each morning.

airport.name: Nadi International Airport (NAN)
airport.drive: 15-20 min to Nadi town/Martintar, 30-40 min to Denarau

tip.r: Tipping is not traditional in Fijian culture and not expected, though appreciated at upscale resorts; some hotels add a discretionary service charge to bills.
